candidates.name: Palazzo d'Accursio
candidates.content: Bologna's city hall, with a very rich collection of Renaissance paintings, sculptures and antique furniture, is a 14th-century palace. Don't miss its enormous main staircase, which was designed to be used by horse drawn carriages.

candidates.name: Museo Civico Archeologico
candidates.hours: Mon, Wed-Fri 09:00-18:00, Sat, Sun and holidays 10:00-19:00
candidates.content: In the Palazzo Galvani – a 14th-century building. This building, an old hospital, houses a comprehensive collection of antiquities from civilizations and cultures including ancient Egypt (mummies and sarcophagi), Iron Age Villanov

candidates.name: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna
candidates.content: Containing the city's most important art, it offers an interesting panorama of the Emilian and Venetian painting from the 13th to the 18th century. A must: the works by Giotto, Raffaello, Parmigianino (Madonna col Bambino/Virgin M

candidates.name: Basilica di San Petronio
candidates.content: It had to be the largest church in the world and in the shape of a huge Latin cross, but was only completed the long arm and with the unfinished façade. The basilica is still one of the most beautiful examples of Italian Gothic st

candidates.name: Museo Morandi
candidates.content: Opened in 1993, the museum houses most of the works by the Bolognese painter Giorgio Morandi.

candidates.name: Museo Ebraico
candidates.hours: Sun-Thu 10:00-18:00, Fri 10:00-16:00. Tickets sold until 17:15 (15:15 Fri). Closed Saturdays and on Jewish holidays
candidates.content: Located in the area of the former ghetto, this museum covers the history of Bologna's Jewish population.

candidates.name: Fontana di Nettuno
candidates.content: A fountain built in 1563 by Tommaso Laureti of Palermo, later embellished by Jean de Boulogne (called Giambologna). It is considered to be one of Bologna’s symbols, and renovated in 2017.

candidates.name: Palazzo dell'Archiginnasio
candidates.hours: Teatro Anatomico & Sala dello Stabat Mater: Mon-Fri 10:00-18:00, Sat 10:00-19:00, Sun 10:00-14:00
candidates.content: Once the main building of the University of Bologna, it houses the Biblioteca comunale dell'Archiginnasio (Archiginnasio Municipal Library). The major attractions of the palace which can be visited are the amazing Teatro Anatomico

candidates.name: Torre degli Asinelli
candidates.content: Closed to the public since October 2023, the tower (built between 1109 and 1119) is 97.20 metres tall (330 feet), with 498 steps and an incline of 1.3 meters (4 feet). Until 2023 you could climb the 498 steps of this tower for spe

candidates.name: Torre Prendiparte
candidates.content: 60-m tower, the second largest in the city. Presumably it used to be higher than its current height. It's a B＆B and room for events, also hosts shows and presentations.

candidates.name: Museo Davia Bargellini
candidates.hours: Tue–Fri 09:00–13:00, Sat Sun holidays 10:00–18:30, Mon closed
candidates.content: A most curious collection, including religious art of the 1500s, a marionette theatre, an 18th-century gilded carriage, and antique keys and door hardware. Housed in a 17th-century palazzo.

candidates.name: International museum and library of music
candidates.alt: Museo Internazionale e Biblioteca della Musica di Bologna
candidates.price: €5, €3 if 65 or older, free if under 18 and on some Th Su
candidates.hours: Museum: Tue–Sun 10:00-18:30, Mon closed; library Tue–Sun 09:30–13:30, Thu also 14:30–16:30
candidates.content: A spectacular collection of music scores, historic instruments, and opera artifacts from 1500 to the early 1900s. There is the first printed score, a 1501 Petrucci. There is the original Clavemusicum Omnitonum of 1606, with 125 ke

candidates.name: Palazzo Poggi
candidates.content: The building houses the headquarters of the University of Bologna. The interior is decorated with frescoes by Pellegrino Tibaldi, on the ground floor is the Hall of Hercules with a statue by Angelo Piò (1730). On the northern side

candidates.name: Museo della Specola
candidates.hours: guided tours only for groups of 15 people max. Tue-Fri at 10:45, 12:15, 15:00, booking by phone; Sat Sun at 11:00, at 15:00, booking online
candidates.content: At the Specola, an astronomical tower built in the beginning of 18th century over Palazzo Poggi. The material exposed illustrates the evolution of the astronomic instrumentation through the centuries.

candidates.name: Museo Europeo degli Studenti
candidates.content: The Museum of European Students is about the history and culture of university students from the thirteenth to the twentieth century. Closed on Monday; Admission free. Don't miss this when you are interested in student life. It's

candidates.name: Museo delle Cere anatomiche "Luigi Cattaneo"
candidates.hours: Jun–Aug: Tue-Fri 10:00-13:00, Sat Sun holiday 10:00-18:00, Mon closed; Sep–May: Tue-Fri 9:00-13:00, Sat Sun holiday 10:00-14:00, Mon closed; closed 1 Jan, 1 May, 15 Aug, 24, 25 Dec
candidates.content: If you think Bologna's towers are crooked, then you'll want to see the deformed spines and diseased oddities at this gross-out Wax Museum. Although dedicated to the history of the art of medical anatomical models of the 19th centu

candidates.name: Orto Botanico ed Erbario
candidates.content: Created in the mid-16th century for medicinal herbs. The Botanical gardens are home to over 5,000 plant species. Some of the highlights include a full-grown sequoia, and a greenhouse for cacti and carnivorous plants.

candidates.name: Palazzo del Podestà
candidates.content: The first seat of the city government.

candidates.name: Palazzo Re Enzo
candidates.content: The palace was built between 1244-1246 as an extension of the nearby Palazzo del Podestà. It takes its name from Enzio of Sardinia, Frederick II's son, who was prisoner here from 1249 until his death in 1272. The current Gothic ap

candidates.name: San Michele in Bosco
candidates.content: Architectural complex comprising the church and adjacent former convent of the Olivetans, with an amazing panoramic view of the city that's great at sunset. Get the number 30 bus if you don't like walking up hills!

candidates.name: Sanctuary of San Luca
candidates.content: Impressive mountain-topped church with a panoramic view which is reachable by a walkway (portico) starting from Porta Saragozza, with over 600 archways - the longest in the world. If you don't want the uphill climb, you can take t

candidates.name: Torre dei Garisenda
candidates.content: Torre dei Garisenda is 47 m (162 feet) tall and has a lean of over 3m (10 feet). It was built in the 12th century.

candidates.name: Torre Azzoguidi
candidates.content: 47 m, built in the 13th century. It's built into the Palazzo del Podestà.

candidates.name: Collezioni Comunali d'Arte
candidates.content: A painting collection of works from various historical periods. Features include works by Giuseppe Maria Crespi (Ritratto del cardinale Lambertini- Portrait of Cardinal Lambertini), Ludovico Carracci (S. Caterina in Carcere – St.

candidates.name: Museo Di Fisica
candidates.hours: during renovation works visits are only by guided tours by appointment

candidates.name: Museo di Mineralogia "Luigi Bombicci"
candidates.content: Rocks, precious stones, rare minerals and meteorites

candidates.name: XM24
candidates.content: An occupied ex-agricultural market where Punk-hc, rock and electronic concerts are often featured. A very cheap place, great if you don't mind the punk atmosphere. Every Thursday from 17:30, it is an organic market. The place also

candidates.name: The Link
candidates.content: A large, 2-floor club that features mostly avant garde electronic, techno and hip-hop gigs and dj-sets. A little book shop, mainly on "alternative" subjects, can be found inside. By bus: Linea 20, 55 or 35.

candidates.name: Covo Club
candidates.content: "storied and legendary Italian indie-punk venue" (Pitchfork), Covo Club is the most renowned indie rock club, features rock djsets and concerts by a number of interesting international bands. Born in 1980, open on Fridays and Satu

candidates.name: Estragon
candidates.content: A big ex-industrial hangar, features dj-sets and concerts by international rock bands almost every night.

candidates.name: TPO
candidates.content: Another occupied location that mostly features experimental music festivals and rock concerts.

candidates.name: VAG61
candidates.content: An historical occupied location that host a wide variety of activities. Every Tuesday from the late afternoon there's an organic market.

candidates.name: Kindergarten
candidates.content: Next to the "Fiera", is a club that features techno, and sometimes punk and new wave concerts.

candidates.name: Bologna Fiere
candidates.content: An Exhibition Centre near Bologna, that among other things has an International Automobile Exhibition every year.

candidates.name: Livello 57
candidates.content: Now only seldom open. It mainly features raves and techno gigs in an industrial, darkish atmosphere.

candidates.name: Ai Vini Scelti
candidates.content: A good enoteca (winery), just outside the center in Via Andrea Costa and only a few moments from Via Pratello, is considered one of the best in Bologna, though there are many others in the center, providing everything from a quick

candidates.name: Locomotiv
candidates.content: Another indie rock club.

candidates.name: Mercato di Mezzo
candidates.content: Great place to have lunch or dinner for a good price. There are different local options for food and tables where you can sit down and enjoy your meal. There are many people at all times of day.

candidates.name: Ristorante Al Pappagallo
candidates.price: €60-90 for first and second courses, or tasting menu (Nov 2019)
candidates.content: It was a famous haunt of the stars during the 1960s and '70s and still attracts an exclusive clientele. Its mix of traditional Bolognese fare and nouvelle cuisine gives the Diana a run for its money. Many other restaurants offer t

candidates.name: Osteria del Sole
candidates.content: If you feel like picnicking on some of the cold cuts (salumi), cheeses and other fresh foods on display in the delicatessens and market stalls off Piazza Maggiore, then Osteria del Sole at a tiny street could be a perfect venue. T

candidates.name: Trattoria Da Vito
candidates.content: Genuine Bolognese fare, from antipasto to dessert, served (occasionally somewhat abruptly) in a down-to-earth trattoria setting popular with locals and visitors alike. Pictures of singer-songwriters such as Lucio Dalla and other l

candidates.name: Tamburini
candidates.content: A reasonably priced self-service lunch. Tamburini is renowned locally as one of Bologna's historic delicatessens, and it also provides a good variety of traditional fare at lunchtime for local employees and other visitors. Queues

candidates.name: Ristorante Diana
candidates.content: It is probably the most famous restaurant in the city but now it is a pale shadow of what it once was, though still high on old world atmosphere. Elderly Bolognese, tourists and businessmen dine here. The traditional regional cuis

candidates.name: Osteria Broccaindosso
candidates.content: Cozy dining room with bolognese traditional dishes, such as tortellini in brodo. Try the mixed vegetables appetiser: a half-dozen bite-sized portions of heaven. The ricotta appetiser melts sweet and soft, like pudding.

candidates.name: L'Antica Trattoria Spiga
candidates.content: A bit hard to find, but make the effort. It has a very good risotto, and wonderful traditional Cucina Bolognese. If you are blessed to visit on a Wednesday, don't miss out on the day's special, a platter with crescente bread serve

candidates.name: Grom
candidates.content: Consistently superb gelato, from the local outpost of an Italian chain. Try the pistachio, and the almond "granita".

candidates.name: I Matti Della Polenta
candidates.content: An unassuming family-run fast food restaurant with delicious, inexpensive polenta in several variations. Get it griglia (grilled), fritta (fried), or spillata. Choose between several sauces, cheeses, and Nutella toppings. Also tig

candidates.name: Trattoria Del Rosso
candidates.content: Traditional Bolognese dishes seven days a week at very reasonable prices. Owned and operated by chef Stefano Curvucci.

candidates.name: Ristorante Teresina
candidates.content: Excellent food. Fish and meat menus, which can change daily, plus a set of traditional Bolognese dishes which are always served.

december.text: Winter can be cold, but Bologna is beautiful the two weeks before Christmas. January and February often feature cloudless blue skies, but the clear weather is often the coldest: you will need a coat, scarf, hat and gloves.
